issues.description: The problem statement's UML specifies that Animal has a constructor with signature Animal(String, int) (name and age), but the solution implementation declares only Animal(String). This mismatch means the solution does not follow the constructor signature required by the specification/tests and would confuse students about the required constructor parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the UML/specification by adding an int age parameter to the Animal constructor (Animal(String name, int age)) and initializing the age field. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to reflect a single-parameter constructor if age is intentionally omitted. Prefer adding the age parameter to the solution so it matches the UML and tests.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Animal has attributes 'name: String' and 'age: int', but the solution's Animal class only defines a 'name' attribute and omits 'age'. This structural difference between specification and solution can confuse students about which attributes they must implement and initialize.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the missing 'private int age;' field to the Animal class in the solution, provide corresponding getter and setter for age, and update the constructor to initialize age according to the UML (Animal(String name, int age)). If the age attribute is intentionally not required, then update the problem statement/UML to remove the age attribute to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) defines Animal with two attributes 'name' and 'age' and a constructor Animal(String, int). The provided solution implementation defines Animal with only a 'name' attribute and a single-argument constructor Animal(String). This mismatch between the problem specification and the actual class/constructor identifiers (presence of 'age' and the two-argument constructor) can confuse students about required attributes and constructor signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and code consistent. Either update the problem statement/UML to remove the 'age' attribute and the two-argument constructor, or modify the template/solution Animal class to include a private int age field with corresponding getter/setter and change the constructor to Animal(String, int) (and update subclasses' constructors to accept and pass an age).
